They are 5-10, the coach is fighting with players, and a starter has already asked for a trade. That doesn’t mean there isn’t talent on the team. In fact, Dumars is being ridiculed because he’s asking for the moon and the stars from other GMs interested in some of his very useful players. That means the Pistons could very well drop a game tonight coming off the high of an absolutely gutsy performance against the San Antonio Spurs. references.title: Attrition finally gets best of Lakers in loss to Jazz
references.excerpt: LOS ANGELES — The Lakers’ league-leading nine-game win streak came to an end in Wednesday’s 109-97 loss to the Utah Jazz. Following a stretch where they seemed unaffected by streaky opponents or a grueling schedule, things finally caught up to them. Legs were heavy, shots came up short, and the Lakers succumbed to an ongoing war of attrition early this season. Los Angeles had its worst offensive game of the season, scoring just 97 points — the lowest since putting up 95 points in the loss to Golden State that ignited its streak — on 34-for-89 (38.2%) shooting from the field and 9-for-33 (27.3%) from range. “Frankly, you’re going to play 82 games, you’re going to have some poor shooting nights,” head coach JJ Redick said postgame. “We’ll take a look at everything, how we can be better offensively.” Redick and the Lakers refused to make an excuse for fatigue, but it evidently affected the way they played. “Who in here feels like they played well tonight,” Redick said he asked the team postgame. No one raised their hand, including Luka Dončić, who has been bearing the weight of the offense all season, which becomes even heavier when Austin Reaves is out. Dončić’s 11-game streak of 30-point games came to an end as the league’s scoring leader scored just 29 points on 28 shot attempts, making just two of his 12 3-point attempts. He also tacked on nine turnovers. “[Fatigue] can’t be an excuse when all NBA teams play 82 games,” Dončić said. “I got to do way better. I know that.”…
